messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] testing code coverage link
parts:
On a complete tangent, but this email reminded me of it: tensor support has been merged into Eigen unsupported: http://listengine.tuxfamily.org/lists.tuxfamily.org/eigen/2015/02/msg00019.html

This is relevant for us as it could a) simplify our mix of arrays and matrices into a single type (reducing duplicated code and complexity of supporting operations on both data types) and b) give us a lot more flexibility with indexing with relative ease.  It may also have other uses with things like kronecker products and who knows what else.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] testing code coverage link
parts:
I saw. I wrote an encouraging note to their list
+1-ing the merge, saying we could use it for third-order
derivative tensors instead of the awkward vector<MatrixXd>.

I hadn't thought about getting rid of our std::vector
style arrays, but that's a great idea. I think they bound
the order, but it'll probably be enough for Stan.

It'll be less efficient for slicing than
std::vector (can't return a reference to a row), but tighter
in memory and better at slicing off columsn if we can get
views working.

If we can reduce code duplication, that'd be a win even
for a small performance hit.

- Bob
